articles.title: Extreme Heat Raises Risk to Babies During Pregnancy, Landmark India Study Finds - Ground Report
articles.search_term: (heatwave OR "heat wave" OR "severe heatwave" OR "extreme heat" OR "heat spell" OR "scorching heat" OR "blistering heat" OR "sweltering heat" OR "hot winds" OR loo OR "hot loo winds" OR "intense heat" OR "unbearable heat" OR "deadly heat" OR heat OR "weather forecast" OR "weather update" OR "weather alert" OR "IMD forecast" OR "IMD prediction" OR "IMD alert" OR IMD OR "rising temperatures" OR "temperatures expected to rise" OR "relief from heat" OR "respite from heat" OR "heat respite" OR "respite from scorching heat") Assam
articles.full_text:
Every extra day of extreme heat a pregnant woman endures in India raises the risk of harm to her baby. That is the finding of the largest study yet to link heat and pregnancy outcomes across the country, and it covers more than 209,000 births.
Researchers tracked births in 707 districts from 2015 to 2020. Long stretches of extreme heat raised the odds of low birth weight, preterm birth, and stillbirth. Timing mattered as much as severity: heat in the first trimester raised preterm birth risk, heat in the second trimester lowered birth weight, and heat in the third trimester carried the strongest link to stillbirth.
Scientists at the University of Queensland–Indian Institute of Technology Delhi Academy of Research led the work, with IIT Delhi, the University of Queensland, the University of New South Wales, the University of Exeter, and Korea University. Environmental Research Communications published the study.
How the Study Measured Heat
Earlier research leaned on average or peak temperatures. This team counted consecutive “sweltering” days — days when the India Heat Index, which combines temperature, humidity, wind speed, and sunlight, climbed above the 90th percentile for that area’s climate history.
Researchers matched hourly heat data to each mother’s exact pregnancy window, using her household location, then adjusted for air pollution, cooking fuel, wealth, education, maternal age, weight, and anemia. The final sample held 209,266 births from India’s National Family Health Survey.
The Numbers
Low birth weight affected 12.8% of the births, the most common problem. Preterm birth affected 1%; stillbirth, 0.74%.
Each additional sweltering day raised the odds of low birth weight by about 1%, after adjustment for other factors.
“While the per-day increase is small, it compounds over a long, hot pregnancy and affects a very large population,” said Vineetha Vincent, the study’s lead author at UQIDAR.
Who Faces the Greatest Risk
The danger fell unevenly. Mothers with a low body mass index — under 18.5 — faced a sharply higher risk of low birth weight from heat than mothers of normal weight.
Women in mountainous regions faced the highest risk from prolonged heat, likely because their bodies are less acclimated to extreme conditions. Low birth weight was also strongly linked to heat in humid subtropical and arid regions.
Poorer households and mothers with little or no schooling faced higher risks of low birth weight and stillbirth as heat exposure rose.
“The mothers most exposed to extreme heat are often those with the fewest resources to cope with it: the poorest, the least educated, the under-nourished,” said Sagnik Dey, co-author and professor at IIT Delhi. “Any adaptation response that ignores this social gradient will miss the women who need protection most.”
Why Heat Harms a Pregnancy
Pregnancy already strains the body. Cardiac output rises by 30% to 50% by late pregnancy, and core temperature shifts.
Extreme heat pushes that temperature higher still. Researchers point to two pathways of harm: rising fetal temperature, which can affect development, and dehydration, which cuts blood flow to the uterus and can trigger early contractions.
Other research backs the pattern. A 2023 Chinese cohort study of more than 205,000 births found that temperatures near the 95th percentile in the week before delivery sharply raised preterm labor risk. A 2024 South Asian cohort study found pregnant women doing physically demanding work in high heat faced double the risk of miscarriage.
What Comes Next
The authors want pregnant women named as a priority group in India’s city heat action plans, with cooling, hydration support, and antenatal advice reaching high-risk districts.
“India already has heat action plans in several cities,” said Nicholas J. Osborne, co-author and researcher at the University of Queensland’s School of Public Health. “The next step is to make sure pregnant women are named as a priority group within them.”
The team is calling for cohort studies that track pregnant women over time and collect biological data, to map exactly how heat damages a developing pregnancy — before India’s summers get hotter still. A related multi-center effort, the Heat in Pregnancy study, is already under way in India.

articles.title: Brace for another heatwave: Only a few cooler days left before extreme heat returns to Hungary - Daily News Hungary
articles.search_term: (heatwave OR "heat wave" OR "severe heatwave" OR "extreme heat" OR "heat spell" OR "scorching heat" OR "blistering heat" OR "sweltering heat" OR "hot winds" OR loo OR "hot loo winds" OR "intense heat" OR "unbearable heat" OR "deadly heat" OR heat OR "weather forecast" OR "weather update" OR "weather alert" OR "IMD forecast" OR "IMD prediction" OR "IMD alert" OR IMD OR "rising temperatures" OR "temperatures expected to rise" OR "relief from heat" OR "respite from heat" OR "heat respite" OR "respite from scorching heat") Assam
articles.full_text:
Hungary has only a few days of relatively comfortable summer weather left before another long-lasting heatwave arrives, according to medium-range weather forecasts.
Forecasters say temperatures will begin rising steadily from next Tuesday, with early August expected to bring widespread highs above 35°C, while some areas could once again see temperatures close to 40°C. According to weather portal Időkép, current forecast models indicate that the hot spell could continue until at least 7 August, with no significant cooling in sight.
Pleasant weekend before the heat returns
Saturday is expected to be mostly sunny across Hungary, with only occasional thin and fair-weather clouds. No rainfall is forecast, and afternoon temperatures should reach 25–30°C, offering ideal conditions for outdoor activities.
Sunday will start with another relatively cool morning, with temperatures between 9°C and 19°C. During the afternoon, cloud cover will increase from the west, bringing scattered showers and thunderstorms first to western Hungary before spreading towards central and eastern parts of the country later in the day.
Strong southerly and south-westerly winds are expected in many areas, particularly across Transdanubia and central Hungary, while thunderstorms may produce locally severe gusts. Afternoon highs will range between 29°C and 34°C.
Heat builds rapidly next week
A cold front passing through on Monday may still trigger isolated showers and thunderstorms. However, meteorologists expect weather patterns to change quickly afterwards.
From Tuesday onwards, south-westerly airflows are forecast to bring increasingly hot air into the Carpathian Basin, causing temperatures to climb day by day.
According to Időkép, the first days of August are expected to bring persistent daytime temperatures well above 35°C across most of Hungary, with some locations potentially reaching or even exceeding 40°C.
Tropical nights expected to return
The heat will not be limited to daytime hours. Forecasters also expect nights to become progressively warmer, making restful sleep increasingly difficult. From the second half of next week,
temperatures in many parts of the country may remain above 20°C overnight, meeting the definition of so-called tropical nights.
Drought conditions likely to worsen
The returning heatwave is also expected to intensify Hungary’s ongoing drought. With scorching sunshine and little or no rainfall forecast for several consecutive days, soil moisture levels are likely to deteriorate further.
As Daily News Hungary reported, according to the latest data from HungaroMet, 90.2% of Hungary is currently experiencing at least moderate agricultural drought, highlighting the growing pressure on crops and water resources after an already exceptionally dry summer.

articles.full_text:
OpenAI oo sheegtay in sirdoonkeeda AI uu xakamaha goostay isla markaana fuliyay weerar dhanka internetka ah oo "aan hore loo arag"
Article Information
Author, Laura Cress
Role, Weriye dhanka tiknoolajiyadda ah
Published
Waqtiga akhriska: 5 daqiiqo
Shirkadda OpenAI ayaa sheegtay in qaar ka mid ah moodelladeeda ugu horumarsan ee sirdoonka macmalka ah (AI) ay ka baxeen xakamaynta intii lagu jiray tijaabo amni, isla markaana ay u suurtagashay inay galaan nidaamyada shirkad billow ah.
Shirkadda samaysay ChatGPT ayaa sheegtay in qeybtan — oo ah nidaam awood u leh inuu si madax-bannaan u fuliyo hawlo marka uu qofku siiyo amar — lagu tijaabinayay deegaan si adag loo xakameeyay. Hase yeeshee, markii uu ogaaday meelaha nugul ee nidaamka, wuxuu awooday inuu ka gudbo xayndaabyadii iyo xaddidaaddii loo dejiyay tijaabada.
Intii ay tijaabadu socotay, AI-gu wuxuu bartilmaameedsaday shirkadda Hugging Face, oo ka mid ah baraha ugu waaweyn adduunka ee lagu wadaago laguna horumariyo moodellada sirdoonka macmalka ah, wuxuuna ku guuleystay inuu galo qaar ka mid ah nidaamyadeeda gudaha.
OpenAI ayaa dhacdadan ku tilmaantay "mid aan hore loo arag", waxayna sheegtay inay si wadajir ah ula shaqaynayso Hugging Face si loo baaro waxa dhacay.
Dhanka kale, Clément Delangue, madaxa fulinta (CEO) ee Hugging Face, ayaa qoraal uu ku daabacay barta X ku yiri: "Wax\a runtii la yaabka leh waa in dhammaan arrimahan ay si toos ah oo iskood ah u dhaceen."
Clément Delangue ayaa sheegay: "Baaritaanku wali wuu socdaa, waxaana soo saari doonnaa macluumaad dheeraad ah oo ku saabsan waxa u muuqda inuu noqon karo dhacdadii ugu horreysay ee noocan ah."
Afhayeen u hadlay dowladda Boqortooyada Midowday (UK) ayaa sheegay in Machadka Ammaanka Sirdoonka Macmalka ah (AI Security Institute) ee dalkaasi uu baarayo hab-dhaqankii nidaamka AI-ga ee dhacdadan ku lug lahaa. Wuxuu intaa ku daray in machadku uu sii wadi doono la shaqaynta OpenAI iyo shaybaarrada kale ee ka shaqeeya sirdoonka macmalka ah si loo xoojiyo tallaabooyinka amniga iyo ilaalinta.
Waxa kale oo ay sheegeen in hay'adaha iyo shirkaduhu ay tahay inay sare u qaadaan awooddooda difaaca internetka, iyagoo qaadaya tallaabooyin ay ka mid yihiin helitaanka shahaadada Cyber Essentials, oo ah barnaamij ay taageerto dowladda UK, kaas oo loogu talagalay in lagu xoojiyo difaaca ka dhanka ah weerarrada internetka.
Warbixinada qotada dheer iyo wararka BBC Somali oo toos kuugu imanaaya WhatsApp.
Halkaan kaga soo biir
Dhamaadka xayeysiinta
Gina Neff, oo ah madaxa Xarunta Tiknoolajiyadda iyo Dimuqraadiyadda Minderoo ee Jaamacadda Cambridge, ayaa u sheegtay barnaamijka Today ee idaacadda BBC Radio 4 in tijaabooyinka amniga caadi ahaan lagu sameeyo "deegaanno ammaan ah", ama waxa loo yaqaan "sandbox". Kuwani waa deegaanno xaddidan oo loogu talagalay in lagu tijaabiyo laguna qiimeeyo awoodaha moodellada sirdoonka macmalka ah (AI) iyada oo aan khatar loo gelin nidaamyada dhabta ah.
Waxay intaas ku dartay:
"Waxay u muuqataa in dhacdadan, OpenAI aysan awoodin inay abuurto sandbox amnigiisu ku filan yahay."
Halkii ay ku ekaan lahaayeen deegaanka tijaabada, AI agent-yadu waxay weerar dhanka internetka ah ku qaadeen isla sandbox-kii, waxayna heleen nuglaansho (vulnerability) u saamaxday inay ka baxaan xaddidaadihii lagu xiray.
Markii ay ka baxeen deegaankaas, AI-gu wuxuu ogaaday in Hugging Face ay u badan tahay inay tahay meesha laga heli karo jawaabihii uu tijaabadu raadinayay, sidaas darteedna wuxuu isku dayay inuu galo qaar ka mid ah nidaamyada gudaha ee shirkadda.
Dhanka kale, Neil Lawrence, oo ah borofisar ku takhasusay barashada mashiinnada (Machine Learning) kana tirsan Jaamacadda Cambridge, ayaa ku tilmaamay dhacdadan "guul farsamo oo cajiib ah", balse wuxuu ka digay in awooddan aysan ka baxsanayn waxa hore loogu yaqaanay moodellada casriga ah ee AI-da.
Wuxuu sidoo kale sheegay in OpenAI ay isku diyaarinayso inay gasho suuqa saamiyada (stock market), isla markaana ay wajahdo tartan xooggan oo uga imanaya shirkadda Anthropic, taas oo si weyn loogu hadal hayo qalabkeeda AI ee awoodda badan ee Mythos.
Lawrence wuxuu yiri:
"OpenAI hadda waxay isku dayaysaa inay dib u soo ceshato kaalinteedii, waxayna doonaysaa inay muujiso awoodda nidaamyadeeda ee dhinaca amniga internetka."
Laakiin wuxuu raaciyay:
"Dhacdadan waxay muujinaysaa in OpenAI weli aysan awoodin inay tiknoolajiyadeeda si buuxda oo ammaan ah u maamusho."
War-saxaafadeedkii ugu horreeyay ee Hugging Face, oo la daabacay 16-kii Luulyo, ayaa lagu sheegay in shirkaddu ay wali baarayso in xogta macaamiisheeda ama la-hawlgalayaasheeda ganacsi ay saameyn soo gaartay iyo in kale. Waxay intaas ku dartay inay la xiriiri doonto cid kasta oo ay dhibaatadu saamaysay haddii loo baahdo.
Shirkaddu waxay sidoo kale sheegtay inay hadda xirtay dhammaan nuglaanshihii la ogaaday intii ay dhacdadani socotay, isla markaana dib u dhistay nidaamyadii ay saameysay.
War-saxaafaddu waxay ku adkaysatay: "Qalabka weerarrada iskiis u fuliya ee ku salaysan sirdoonka macmalka ah (AI) hadda ma aha oo kaliya mala-awaal ama fikrad aragtiyeed."
Waxay sii raacisay: "Difaaca aaladaha internetka wuxuu hadda u baahan yahay in xogta iyo moodellada AI loo arko bartilmaameedyo waaweyn oo weerarro lagu qaadi karo, isla markaana AI lafteeda loo adeegsado difaac si loola jaanqaado khataraha isa soo taraya."
Ugu dambayn, Hugging Face waxay sheegtay inay sii wadi doonto maalgelinta dhinacan, isla markaana ay la wadaagi doonto bulshada aqoonta iyo casharrada ay ka barato.
Dhacdo digniin weyn ah
Dhacdadan ayaa mar kale dhalisay su'aalo ku saabsan awoodaha nidaamyada casriga ah ee sirdoonka macmalka ah (AI) iyo in tallaabooyinka amniga ee hadda jira ay weli ku filan yihiin iyo in kale, iyadoo tiknoolajiyadani sii xoogaysanayso.
Spencer Starkey, oo ka mid ah madaxda shirkadda amniga internetka ee SonicWall, ayaa BBC-da u sheegay in dhacdadani si cad u muujinayso in hay'aduhu ay tahay inay kor u qaadaan difaacooda dhanka internetka isla markaana adkeysiga amniga internetka ka dhigaan mid ka mid ah mudnaantooda ugu weyn.
Wuxuu yiri: "Xaqiiqada murugada leh ayaa ah in ururro badan ay weli isku difaacayaan xawaare bini'aadan, halka weeraryahannadu ay ku socdaan xawaare mashiin."
Dhanka kale, Travis Lele, oo ah injineer sare oo amniga ka tirsan shirkadda la-talinta amniga internetka ee GuidePoint Security, ayaa ku tilmaamay horumarkan: "Waa waqti digniin weyn u ah amniga internetka."
Wuxuu intaas ku daray: "Dhacdadan waxay muujinaysaa isu-dheelitir la'aanta hore loo ogaa."
Isagoo sharaxaya ayuu yiri: "AI-da weerarrada fulisa kuma xirna xaddidaado badan, halka qalabka ugu horumarsan ee difaaca ay weli ku tiirsan yihiin nidaamyo aan si buuxda u fahmi karin macnaha iyo duruufaha ay wax ku dhacayaan."
Si kastaba ha ahaatee, Jake Moore, oo ah la-taliye caalami ah oo dhinaca amniga internetka ka tirsan shirkadda ESET, ayaa sheegay in ku dhawaaqista dhacdadan ay sidoo kale yeelan karto ujeeddo tartan ganacsi.
Sida uu qabo, OpenAI waxaa laga yaabaa inay doonayso inay muujiso awoodda tiknoolajiyadeeda AI, xilli shirkadda la tartanta ee Anthropic ay si isa soo taraysa u soo jiidanayso dareenka iyadoo adeegsanaysa moodalkeeda Claude Mythos.
Moore wuxuu yiri: "Soo bandhigista dhacdadan waxay dhalinaysaa su'aasha ah in OpenAI ay isku dayayso inay gaarto guushii xayeysiineed ee Anthropic ay dhawaan heshay."
Warbixintan ayaa la daabacay hal toddobaad kadib markii shirkadda cusub ee Shiinaha ee Moonshot AI ay soo bandhigtay Kimi K3, oo ah moodal aad u weyn oo sirdoon macmal ah. Shirkaddu waxay sheegtay in Kimi K3 uu awood u leeyahay inuu la tartamo moodellada ugu sarreeya ee ay sameeyaan shirkadaha waaweyn ee Mareykanka.

articles.title: HVAC companies prepare for another weekend of extreme heat - InForum
articles.search_term: (heatwave OR "heat wave" OR "severe heatwave" OR "extreme heat" OR "heat spell" OR "scorching heat" OR "blistering heat" OR "sweltering heat" OR "hot winds" OR loo OR "hot loo winds" OR "intense heat" OR "unbearable heat" OR "deadly heat" OR heat OR "weather forecast" OR "weather update" OR "weather alert" OR "IMD forecast" OR "IMD prediction" OR "IMD alert" OR IMD OR "rising temperatures" OR "temperatures expected to rise" OR "relief from heat" OR "respite from heat" OR "heat respite" OR "respite from scorching heat") Assam
articles.full_text:
FARGO — With another weekend of extreme heat in the forecast, air conditioning units across the region are being pushed to their limits.
HVAC companies say they're prepping for a busy few days as more homeowners deal with broken or struggling systems.
ADVERTISEMENT
With a surge in service calls expected, some companies are making sure all of their employees are on the clock and ready to deal with the increased number of calls.
"We like to keep our staff fully staffed going forward in these long hot weekends, just to make sure that when the calls come in, we do get them taken care of in a fast, efficient way," said Ty Rambousek, Laney's business development manager.
A heat wave already swept over the region earlier this month, which brought more calls for service than usual to Laney's in Fargo. To prepare for the next few days of high temperatures, companies are stocking up on parts.
"Well, that's one thing we actually anticipate these type of hot weather spells, so we always try to order a little bit more to make sure our customers get serviced," Rambousek said.
One thing Rambousek recommends is to set your thermostat inside your home to 20 degrees below the temperature outside.
"Your AC is being its most efficient at that 20-degree mark, and you won't have to worry about making it go out or anything like that. If it's 100 degrees out this weekend, set it to 80, and you're not going to overwork your AC," Rambousek said.
If the AC does go out in your home, while you wait for service, Rambousek's recommendation is to try to eliminate any form of sunlight from entering your home.
ADVERTISEMENT
"So, close your blinds in your house. It keeps the temperature at least somewhat cool. If you have a fan, plug that one in and get it going. And just please be patient. We're working through a lot of calls, and we'll get to you," Rambousek said.
If your air conditioner does stop working, technicians recommend calling for service as soon as possible, since appointment schedules can fill up quickly during extended heat waves.
Matthew Freeman has been a reporter for WDAY since 2026. He is a graduate of Dan Patrick's School for Sports Broadcasting at Full Sail University. He is from Panama City Beach, FL.

articles.title: Public Warned to Take Precautions Against Heat-Related Illnesses During Extreme Weather Conditions - bastillepost.com
articles.search_term: (heatstroke OR "heat stroke" OR sunstroke OR "heat exhaustion" OR "heat-related death" OR "heat casualty" OR "heat fatality" OR "suspected heat death" OR dehydration OR "heat cramps" OR "heat illness") Assam
articles.full_text:
DH reminds public to take precautions against heat-related illnesses during very hot weather
The Centre for Health Protection (CHP) of the Department of Health (DH) today (July 25) reminded members of the public to take appropriate precautions against heat-related illnesses, such as heat cramps, heat exhaustion and heat stroke, during very hot weather.
In a high-temperature environment, excessive sweating and difficulty in heat dissipation can cause stress to the body. Members of the public should take the following precautions:
- Hydrate in a timely manner to prevent dehydration;
- Wear light-coloured, loose-fitting and breathable clothing to minimise heat absorption and facilitate perspiration and heat dissipation;
- Keep indoor areas well ventilated and maintain appropriate temperature and humidity, e.g. by opening windows or using a fan or air-conditioning;
- Avoid strenuous exercise and prolonged activities such as hiking or trekking;
- Arrange outdoor activities in the morning or the late afternoon, if possible, and bring enough water; and
- Avoid beverages containing caffeine, such as coffee and tea, as well as alcoholic beverages, which may speed up water loss through the urinary system.
In addition, infants and children, the elderly, pregnant women, individuals with chronic illnesses such as heart disease or high blood pressure, overweight people and outdoor/manual workers are more susceptible to heat stroke. These groups should pay special attention to the following:
- Infants and young children: Avoid going outside when the temperature is high. If they must go outside, adults should ensure they stay in places with moderate temperatures and good ventilation or air-conditioning. Infants and young children should never be left unattended in a confined space such as a vehicle;
- The elderly, pregnant women, individuals with chronic illnesses and overweight people: Pay close attention to health conditions and seek help as soon as possible if experiencing any abnormalities in health indicators such as blood pressure, heart rate, etc or if there are fluctuations in health conditions. Avoid going out when the temperature is high. Make sure there is good ventilation, or turn on a fan or air-conditioner to keep an appropriate temperature indoors. High temperatures can also worsen the condition of people with chronic illnesses (such as cardiovascular and respiratory diseases). Therefore, they should have an ample supply of their usual medication and keep in contact with family members, neighbours and the community. People should seek immediate help if they feel unwell.
- Outdoor/manual workers: Reschedule work to cooler hours as far as feasible. If working in a hot environment is unavoidable, provide shade where practicable and use ventilation and heat dissipation equipment. Once work has begun, gradually adjust the pace of work and take breaks in the shade to regain strength.
The DH reminded the public that heat stroke is one of the most common health risks in hot weather. Over the past five years, there have been over 200 hospital admissions due to heat stroke each year in Hong Kong, with two to five fatal cases occurring mainly during the summer months from May to September. Vulnerable groups are more susceptible to heat stroke. Symptoms include dizziness, headache, nausea, shortness of breath or confusion. In severe cases, patients may suffer from convulsions or become unconscious, which can be life-threatening if they are not cooled down and resuscitated in a timely manner.
Members of the public are also advised to pay attention to the latest weather, as well as the real-time and forecasted ultraviolet (UV) index released by the Hong Kong Observatory (HKO). When the UV index is high (6 or above), the public should note the following:
- Avoid direct sunlight exposure to the skin and the eyes;
- Apply broad-spectrum, water-resistant sunscreen liberally, with a sun protection factor (SPF) of at least 30 or higher, when participating in outdoor activities. Reapply every two hours if staying outdoors for long periods, or after swimming, sweating or towelling off;
- While using DEET-containing insect repellents for personal protection against mosquito-borne diseases, apply sunscreen before insect repellent;
If symptoms develop, such as dizziness, headache, nausea, shortness of breath or confusion, rest and seek help immediately, and seek medical advice as soon as possible.
For more health information, the public may visit theCHP's heat strokepage andUV radiation page; the HKO's Dial-a-Weather (1878 200),latestweather report and forecast,UV Indexand weather information forhiking and mountaineering; andpress releasesof the Labour Departmenton precautions against heat stroke for outdoor workers and their employers when the Heat Stress at Work Warning is in force.

Health risk category for Air Quality Health Index may reach "Serious" level
According to the Environmental Protection Department (EPD)'s forecast, the health risk category of Air Quality Health Index (AQHI) at some air quality monitoring stations may reach the "Serious" level later today (July 25).
The EPD has recorded higher-than-normal air pollution levels in some areas since yesterday (July 24) afternoon. Under the influence of the outer subsiding air of tropical cyclone Noul, the weather in Hong Kong today is fine and very hot with moderate northwesterly winds. Weak winds are unfavourable for pollutant dispersion. The intense sunshine enhances photochemical smog activity, leading to the rapid formation of ozone and fine particulates in the Pearl River Delta region. The high ozone level also promotes the formation of nitrogen dioxide.
According to the Hong Kong Observatory, there will be heavy squally showers with windy conditions tomorrow (July 26). It is expected that air quality in Hong Kong will improve by then.
With a health risk category in the "Very High" range or above, children, the elderly and persons with existing heart or respiratory illnesses are advised to reduce physical exertion and outdoor activities to a minimum or avoid such activities. The general public is advised to reduce, or reduce to a minimum, outdoor physical exertion, and to reduce time outdoors, especially in areas with heavy traffic. As health effects of air pollutants may vary for individuals, persons who are in doubt or experience discomfort should seek advice from healthcare professionals. The public may visit the Centre for Health Protection's website (www.chp.gov.hk/en/content/9/460/3557.html) for more information on health effects of air pollution and relevant health advice.
The Education Bureau (EDB) urges all schools to visit the EDB website for appropriate measures to safeguard students' health and take note of changes in the index. The relevant hyperlink is as follows: www.edb.gov.hk/en/sch-admin/admin/about-activities/sch-activities-guidelines/index.html.
When the air quality health risk category is at the "Very High" level, employers of outdoor workers performing heavy manual work are advised to assess the risk of outdoor work and take appropriate preventive measures to protect the health of their employees, such as reducing outdoor physical exertion and the time of their stay outdoors, especially in areas with heavy traffic. At the "Serious" level, employers of all outdoor workers are advised to assess the risk of outdoor work and take appropriate preventive measures to protect the health of their employees.

ARAPAHOE COUNTY, Colo. — At the Arapahoe County Fair, vendors and staff are doing what they can to stay safe through a long, hot weekend — and they want fairgoers to do the same.
▶️ Denver7's Arapahoe County Reporter Adria Iraheta spoke with vendors ahead of a hot weekend at the fair
Beating the heat at the Arapahoe County Fair
Dizziness, cramping, heavy sweating and a rapid heartbeat are signs of heat-related illness to watch for this weekend if you plan on spending extended time outdoors.
With triple-digit temperatures expected, health officials warn that dehydration, heat exhaustion and heat stroke are serious risks.
Marion Thompson, a game operator at the fair, said the shade at his booth doubles as a selling point.
"I tell people to drink a lot of water when they come by and make sure like, hey, come in the shade and play the game," Thompson said.
His personal strategy for getting through the day is simple.
"I stay in the shades, drink a lot of water, say my prayers," Thompson said.
On the other side of the fairgrounds, Mirasol Black is running the Taste of Lumpia food truck, serving Filipino food including lumpia, pancit and pork barbecue. Working next to a fryer that pushes temperatures inside the truck to between 100 and 105 degrees makes the job especially grueling.
"Triple digits. It's gonna be a lot," Black said.
A popsicle handed to her during a break offered a welcome cool-down.
"Oh, hydrate. Lots of water. Water, water. Oh, I just got handed. I didn't say tangerine, but yeah, this is the popsicle. So that'll help you cool off a little. Yes, popsicle," Black said.
Arapahoe County Open Spaces Director Gini Pingeno said the fair is taking the heat seriously and wants attendees to do the same.
"We're very invested in people being cognizant of how hot they're getting and making sure that they're doing things they need to do to cool down and continue to enjoy the wonderful things the fair has to offer," Pingeno said.
The fair is handing out cooling towels to the first 1,200 guests each day. For those who miss the giveaway, misting stations, water slides and indoor exhibits are also available.
"We really do encourage people to spend some time outside and then go inside and cool off," Pingeno said.
Despite the heat, both Thompson and Black say the long days are worth it.
"You know, that heat really do wonders for us because it brings people, a lot of people in and in the shade, and they want to play," Thompson said.
Black agreed, saying the smiles on customers' faces make it all worthwhile.
"It was worth it... Yes, worth the heat," Black said.

Rescuers aid dehydrated hiker on muggy Mount Hood day
Published 1:15 pm Friday, July 24, 2026
A pair of hikers on a two-day journey from Timberline Lodge down to the Zigzag Mountain Trailhead got some help from search and rescue after running out of water on a scorching hot day.
Wednesday, July 22, search and rescue volunteers deployed to aid a dehydrated hiker on the Zigzag Mountain Trail. The 56-year-old man was on an outing with his 34-year-old daughter. After camping overnight, the man ran out of water Wednesday morning — during the start of one of the hottest, muggiest days of the year.
That afternoon, just before 3:30 p.m., he succumbed to the heat and became disoriented and unable to continue walking. It was likely a combination of dehydration and heat exhaustion. So his daughter called 911.
Hoodland Fire, AMR, and Clackamas Search & Rescue deployed to their location. They reached the father-daughter duo around 4:30 p.m. several switchbacks up from the trailhead. They gave the man IV fluids, and a wheeled litter was brought in case he needed additional aid.
After he was rehydrated and rested, the man was able to slowly walk to the trailhead accompanied by rescuers. While they walked a Clackamas Search & Rescue team member carried an IV connected to the man. The group made it back to the parking lot just before 7 p.m.
“This rescue has a happy ending but also offers a few teachable moments,” rescuers wrote. “Make sure you plan ahead for the weather, and plan for the worst — bringing plenty of food, water, and electrolytes.”
Email newsletter signup
There is a difference between heat exhaustion and heatstroke:
Heat exhaustion includes heavy sweating, dizziness, nausea, muscle cramps and cool/pale/clammy skin. If you see those signs, move to a cool place, loosen clothing, apply wet cloths to your body, and sip water. Seek medical help if you begin vomiting or if symptoms worsen.
Heatstroke is a life-threatening emergency. Signs include high body temperature (above 103 degrees), hot and red skin, confusion, a fast and strong pulse, and losing consciousness. If you suspect heatstroke, call 911 immediately.

Typhoon Noul to make landfall along Guangdong coast, orange alert renewed
By Xinhua
BEIJING – The National Meteorological Center renewed an orange typhoon alert at 6 pm Friday as Typhoon Noul, the 12th typhoon of the year, is expected to make landfall along the coast of South China's Guangdong province between Saturday evening and Sunday morning.
Typhoon Noul was upgraded from tropical storm to severe tropical storm on Friday afternoon. After making landfall between Zhuhai and Raoping in Guangdong, the typhoon will turn northward and gradually weaken, the center said.
From 8 pm Friday to 8 pm Saturday, parts of eastern Guangdong and Taiwan are expected to experience heavy to torrential rain due to the typhoon, with some areas in southeastern Taiwan possibly seeing downpours.
Strong winds are expected in parts of the South China Sea, the Bashi Channel, the waters east of Taiwan, the Taiwan Strait, the southern East China Sea, as well as the coastal areas of Taiwan, Fujian and Guangdong.
China has a four-tier, color-coded weather warning system for typhoons, with red representing the most severe warning, followed by orange, yellow and blue.
In response to Typhoon Noul, the State Flood Control and Drought Relief Headquarters on Friday activated a Level-IV emergency response for flooding and typhoon control in Guangdong and Fujian, and dispatched a work team to Guangdong for guidance.
On the same day, the Ministry of Emergency Management launched a Level-IV emergency response for geological disasters in the two provinces.
To safeguard agricultural production against potential risks, the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs has recently taken a series of measures, which include guiding affected areas to speed up the harvesting of crops and aquaculture products and to reinforce planting and breeding facilities.
